page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highmem-8-lssd is a network-optimized virtual machine profile designed for memory-intensive enterprise tasks requiring rapid local input/output. Built on a 64-bit x86 architecture, the instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs backed by 62 GB of system memory, delivering a generous allocation of 7.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. It operates without hardware acceleration GPUs and allocates no complimentary public IPv4 addresses, directing primary utility toward internal backend execution.

Integrated directly into the instance configuration is 403 GB of high-speed local NVMe solid-state storage. By physically attaching local NVMe SSD capacity to the compute host, the instance achieves low latency and sustained high throughput for transient data, eliminating standard network-attached storage latency. However, local storage remains ephemeral, necessitating external replication or persistent disk integration to safeguard against host maintenance interruptions.

From an architectural efficiency perspective, the c4n-highmem-8-lssd presents an attractive density profile for organizations requiring high RAM-to-core ratios alongside high-throughput local disk storage. By combining dedicated CPU resource isolation, ample memory headroom, and bundled NVMe media, the instance reduces compute footprint requirements for workloads that would otherwise require overprovisioning core counts simply to secure memory or fast disk access.

The hardware configuration makes the c4n-highmem-8-lssd well aligned for in-memory databases, real-time analytics nodes, caching layers, distributed message brokers, and transactional data processing environments that rely heavily on low-latency local scratch space.
